newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere could buy 49pct of Dasa missiles.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere could buy 49pct of Dasa missiles.

text.p: Lagardere Groupe's Matra BAe Dynamics unit has an option to buy up to 49 percent of LFK, the missiles subsidiary of Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), as part of an agreement signed between the French and German firms, Lagardere said on Tuesday.

Lagardere and Dasa signed "binding agreements" on May 7, to form strategic alliances on their space and missiles activities, Noel Forgeard, chairman and chief executive of Matra High Technology, told journalists.

The missiles accord gives the Matra BAe Dynamics 50/50 joint venture with British Aerospace Plc a pre-emptive right to take an initital planned 30 percent stake in LFK and up to 49 percent within 2-1/2 years, if Dasa chooses to sell it to a foreign firm, Forgeard said.
The agreement on space activities will see the creation of a joint venture between Matra Marconi Space (MMS), in which Lagardere owns 51 percent and General Electric Co Plc 49 percent, and Dasa.

MMS will hold between 60-70 percent of the new company which will rank third in the world market with annual sales of $3 billion after Lockheed Martin's $7 billion and the merged Boeing McDonnell Douglas, which has $5 billion.
The Dasa alliance will boost MMS' annual sales to 15 billion francs ($2.6 billion) from 1996's 8.4 billion, said MMS Chief Executive Armand Carlier.

The German accords will boost annual sales of the Matra High Technology division, which includes defence, space and information systems, to 33 billion francs from 1996 turnover of 26.6 billion, Forgeard said.
The aim is to build "an integrated European entity" to confront the U.S. giants in space and defence, he said.

The "irreversible agreements" with Dasa are not conditional on Lagardere's bid in the Thomson-CSF privatisation and were based on industrial logic which Lagardere has consistently pursued over the last two years, he said.

Whatever the composition of France's new government, it would have to take account the new Lagardere-Dasa grouping. He saw no reason why the alliances should not receive official approval. The alliances "protect French interests" by maintaining French control and an integrated management, he said.

Forgeard said if the Socialists formed a new government he hoped the Thomson-CSF privatisation would go ahead as there was no reason why France should stay in the "ghetto" of a state-owned defence industry when those in the United States, Britain and other countries were in the private sector.

GEC had been informed and taken part in the MMS-Dasa talks and its silence since the alliance announcement, which has been noticed by industry observers, should be interpreted as agreement with the deal, he said.
Given GEC's culture of creating shareholder value, it was difficult to see an alternative to the Dasa alliance, he said.
Forgeard was speaking to journalists ahead of a two-day tour of Matra's missiles and space activities in Britain and France.

LFK has annual sales of around 900 million marks ($531.4 million) in missiles and guided weapons. Matra BAe Dynamics 1996 turnover was 8.1 billion francs. ($ = 1.693 German Marks) ($ = 5.715 French Francs)
